_meta.source: FDA regulations (21 CFR), EFSA decisions, EU Regulation 1333/2008
_meta.how_to_update: Add new entries with name, jurisdiction, action, year, and regulation fields. Check FDA Federal Register notices and EFSA Journal for updates.

banned_or_restricted.name: Brominated vegetable oil (BVO)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Final rule effective August 2024

banned_or_restricted.name: Partially hydrogenated oils (trans fats)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Artificial trans fats removed from food supply

banned_or_restricted.name: Red No. 3 (Erythrosine, E127)
banned_or_restricted.regulation: Final rule January 2025; compliance by January 2027
banned_or_restricted.notes: Delaney clause — shown to cause cancer in animals

banned_or_restricted.name: Red No. 2 (Amaranth, E123)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Suspected carcinogen

banned_or_restricted.name: Red No. 4 (Scarlet GN)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Adrenal gland damage in dogs

banned_or_restricted.name: Orange No. 1
banned_or_restricted.notes: Organ damage in studies

banned_or_restricted.name: Cyclamate
banned_or_restricted.notes: Bladder cancer in rats. Still approved in EU and 55+ countries.

banned_or_restricted.name: Safrole
banned_or_restricted.notes: Hepatocarcinogen. Naturally occurs in sassafras, formerly used in root beer.

banned_or_restricted.name: Coumarin
banned_or_restricted.notes: Liver toxicity. Naturally present in cinnamon (cassia variety).

banned_or_restricted.name: Dulcin
banned_or_restricted.notes: Artificial sweetener — liver carcinogen

banned_or_restricted.name: Thiourea
banned_or_restricted.notes: Carcinogen, previously used in citrus fruit packaging

banned_or_restricted.name: Diethylstilbestrol (DES)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Synthetic estrogen, growth promoter

banned_or_restricted.name: Calamus (Acorus calamus)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Contains beta-asarone, a carcinogen

banned_or_restricted.name: Boric acid / Borax
banned_or_restricted.notes: Toxic. Banned in 1920s, briefly reinstated during WWII, permanently banned 1950s.

banned_or_restricted.name: Azodicarbonamide (ADA)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Flour treatment agent. Still FDA-approved in US (21 CFR 172.806) at ≤45 ppm.

banned_or_restricted.name: Potassium bromate
banned_or_restricted.notes: Flour treatment agent. IARC 2B. Not formally banned by FDA but industry has largely removed it. California Prop 65 listed.

banned_or_restricted.name: Titanium dioxide (E171)
banned_or_restricted.action: No longer authorized as food additive
banned_or_restricted.notes: EFSA 2021: can no longer be considered safe. Still FDA-approved in US.

banned_or_restricted.name: Fast Yellow AB (E105)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Banned in both EU and US

banned_or_restricted.name: Patent Blue V (E131)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Approved in EU. Not permitted in US or Australia.

banned_or_restricted.name: Green S (E142)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Approved in EU. Not permitted in US or Japan.

banned_or_restricted.name: Vegetable carbon (E153)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Approved in EU.

banned_or_restricted.name: Biphenyl (E230)
banned_or_restricted.notes: Formerly used as fruit preservative

banned_or_restricted.name: Allura Red AC (E129)
banned_or_restricted.action: Banned by Austria, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Sweden, Norway, Switzerland
banned_or_restricted.notes: Still approved at EU level. Southampton Six member.

southampton_six.source: EU Regulation 1333/2008, Annex V — McCann et al., The Lancet, 2007
southampton_six.notes: Products containing these must carry: 'may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children'
